title: Balanced contraction on sheaf tensors
statement: Let $Z$ be a topological space, $R,B$ sheaves of commutative rings, and $\alpha:R\to B$ a unital morphism. Let $M$ be a $B$-module sheaf and $N$ an $R$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Put $H=\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}$ and $E=(U\mapsto B(U)\otimes_{R(U)}N(U))^\#$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Write $p_R,p_B$ for the pure tensor maps and $\eta$ for the sheafification unit. There exists an $R$-module-sheaf morphism $\psi:H(M\otimes_B E)\to H(M)\otimes_R N$ such that for every open $U$ and sections $m,b,n$, $\psi(p_B(m,\eta(b\otimes n)))=p_R(bm,n)$. No inverse identity is part of this assertion, and there are no flatness, finiteness or nonzero assumptions.

source.place: Tag 08DE, proof, ordinary balanced identity; Tag 0GMW, tensor and sheafification. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08DE and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GMW.

proof.text: Construct the section contraction with Mathlib TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange, restricting its linear equivalence to R(U). Its pure tensor formula is (b m) tensor n. Two tensor inductions show naturality: restrictions preserve multiplication, and restriction of b m is restriction(b) restriction(m).

Restriction of scalars commutes with sheafification up to the canonical map extending the restricted B-sheafification unit. Forget to abelian sheaves: both associated objects are the same sheafification, and the underlying comparison is the identity by the abelian adjunction. The forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms.

Tensor M.val with the sheafification unit of the extension presheaf. This unit is inverted by sheafification and W_whiskerLeft preserves this property. Sheafify and compose with tensorObjIsoSheafification.inv, obtaining an isomorphism from the sheafification of the original balanced presheaf tensor onto M tensor_B E.

Restrict this isomorphism, invert it and the preceding restriction-sheafification comparison, then compose with R-sheafification of the presheaf contraction and tensorObjIsoSheafification.inv. Naturality of the two units and the section contraction formula give exactly the stated section formula.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_balancedTensorContraction (α : R ⟶ B)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (𝓡 B)) (N : SheafOfModules.{u} (𝓡 R)) :
    ∃ ψ : (restrictScalars (𝓻 α)).obj
        ((monoidalCategory B).tensorObj M (changeOfRings.{u, u, u} α N)) ⟶
      (monoidalCategory R).tensorObj ((restrictScalars (𝓻 α)).obj M) N,
      ∀ (W : (Opens Z)ᵒᵖ) (m : M.val.obj W) (b : B.obj.obj W) (n : N.val.obj W),
      ψ.val.app W
        ((tensorObjIsoSheafification M (changeOfRings.{u, u, u} α N)).inv.val.app W
        (((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 (𝓡 B).obj)).unit.app
          (M.val ⊗ (changeOfRings.{u, u, u} α N).val)).app W
            (m ⊗ₜ[B.obj.obj W]
              ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 (𝓡 B).obj)).unit.app
                (changeOfRingsPresheaf.{u, u, u} α N)).app W
                  (b ⊗ₜ[R.obj.obj W,(α.hom.app W).hom] n)))) =
      (tensorObjIsoSheafification ((restrictScalars (𝓻 α)).obj M) N).inv.val.app W
        (((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 (𝓡 R).obj)).unit.app
          (((restrictScalars (𝓻 α)).obj M).val ⊗ N.val)).app W
            ((b • m) ⊗ₜ[R.obj.obj W] n))
